\label{lemma-last-one-flat}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ be a bounded above complex of flat
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with tor-amplitude in $[a, b]$.
Then $\Coker(d_{\mathcal{E}^\bullet}^{a - 1})$ is a flat
$\mathcal{O}_X$-module.

statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$ with $a \leq b$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ has tor-amplitude in $[a, b]$.
\item $E$ is represented by a complex
$\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ of flat $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with
$\mathcal{E}^i = 0$ for $i \not \in [a, b]$.
\end{enumerate}

Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$ with $a \leq b$.
conclusions:

\item $E$ is represented by a complex
$\mathcal{E}^\bullet$ of flat $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules with
$\mathcal{E}^i = 0$ for $i \not \in [a, b]$.
\end{enumerate}
semantic_review_note: For E∈D(O_X) and integers a≤b, tor-amplitude in [a,b] is equivalent to having a flat complex representative supported in cohomological degrees [a,b]. Both directions, termwise FLAT requirement and exact closed interval are retained.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback}
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$, then $Lf^*E$ has tor amplitude in
$[a, b]$.
statement:
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$, then $Lf^*E$ has tor amplitude in
$[a, b]$.
hypotheses:
Let $f : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed
spaces. Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_Y)$.
conclusions:
If $E$ has tor amplitude in $[a, b]$, then $Lf^*E$ has tor amplitude in
$[a, b]$.
semantic_review_note: Derived pullback Lf* of any object with tor-amplitude [a,b] along a ringed-space morphism has the same tor-amplitude interval [a,b]. The final does not demand flatness of f or claim equality of arbitrary cohomology bounds.

statement:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$ with $a \leq b$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E$ has tor-amplitude in $[a, b]$.
\item for every $x \in X$ the object $E_x$ of $D(\mathcal{O}_{X, x})$
has tor-amplitude in $[a, b]$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses:
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space.
Let $E$ be an object of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$.
Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$ with $a \leq b$.
semantic_review_note: Tor-amplitude [a,b] of a derived O_X-object is a stalkwise criterion: it holds globally exactly when it holds for E_x over O_{X,x} for every x. The final preserves both implications and the universal stalk quantifier.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-summands-tor-amplitude}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ be a ringed space. Let $a, b \in \mathbf{Z}$.
For $K$, $L$ objects of $D(\mathcal{O}_X)$ if $K \oplus L$ has tor
amplitude in $[a, b]$ so do $K$ and $L$.
